home.headline: RAMAHAZOMANANA Mandrindra Antonnio — software developer
home.subhead: Backend-first, full-stack in practice — NestJS, FastAPI, Next.js and PostgreSQL, wrapped in Docker and shipped through CI/CD. Currently completing an M1 in Computer Science while building and shipping production systems.
home.philosophyBody: Engineering isn't just about writing code — it's about designing solutions built to last. My approach pairs technical discipline with a habit of learning fast: picking up a new stack, framework, or protocol as the project demands it, then proving it in production.
home.principle1Body: Designing systems that stay predictable under load — typed APIs, async data layers, and infrastructure that fails loudly instead of silently.
home.principle2Body: Filling gaps deliberately — from self-taught data structures and algorithms to CTF challenges — to keep pace with problems the curriculum hasn't caught up to yet.

about.headline: Driven by logic, defined by rigor.
about.introTitle: M1 Informatique student building production systems on the side, not just for class.
about.bioP1: I'm an M1 Informatique student on the MISA track at the Université d'Antananarivo, with a fullstack profile centered on backend engineering — NestJS, FastAPI, Next.js, PostgreSQL and Docker, wired together with CI/CD.
about.bioP2: My bachelor's focused on networking — TCP/IP, Linux, packet analysis, so I've been filling that gap deliberately: self-studying algorithms, graph theory and complexity analysis to prepare for research-track ambitions at M2 and beyond.
about.bioP3: Outside coursework, I compete in CTF challenges, play chess, and build in the open — from a full “student OS” monorepo to a CLI that turns plain language into shell commands.
about.philosophyQuote: Good engineering starts with understanding the system, not just shipping the feature.
about.philosophyBody: I'd rather spend an extra hour reading the error than an extra week debugging in production. Simplicity, tested assumptions, and a habit of learning the tool before reaching for it — that's the whole method.
